title: Integration of climate risks in the macroeconomic framework
trigger: BNR publishes a research paper and concept note on climate channels in the Rwandan macro framework, formally integrated into the MPC briefing cycle.
rationale: The Monetary Policy Department confirmed that climate (weather patterns in particular) already enters MPC discussions informally; the November 2025 MPC explicitly flagged a climate-negative scenario that materialised. No formal published research yet except a paper on climate risk for the financial system. BNR Review identified as outlet.

scalable_ambition.advanced: Climate scenarios formally embedded in the Quarterly Projection Model (QPM) documentation.

ta: Short-term specialised (NGFS methodology, peer central bank exchange) and medium-term support (macroeconomic modelling, co-authoring of the paper).
donor_complementarity: No active TA on this exact angle; IMF QPM work covers core forecasting but not climate channels.
fy_26_27: Concept note drafted; team formed; first paper outline approved.
fy_27_28: Paper co-authored and submitted to BNR Review; preliminary climate scenarios in MPC briefing.
fy_28_29: Paper published; climate scenarios formally integrated into QPM documentation.
rsf_fsap_link: Complements IMF RSF reform agenda on climate macro framework.
risks: Dependence on meteorological agency data quality

title: Climate-augmented macroeconomic forecasting
trigger: BNR extends its forecasting horizon beyond 1 month for weather-sensitive variables by integrating satellite imagery and ESTEEM model outputs into the QPM.
rationale: BNR model currently capped at 1M (meteorology agency limit); data science team already uses satellite imagery for agri estimates. AFD ESTEEM mission (June) on floods/landslides is the natural anchor. Bridges a tangible data gap.

scalable_ambition.baseline: Pilot integration of satellite data into one model module.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Full climate-augmented QPM with extended horizon, gazetted as MPC reference.

ta: Mixed — short-term modelling expertise + long-term capacity building for the analysis and research divisions.
donor_complementarity: Builds directly on AFD ESTEEM; Green PFM II adds the 'absorption' layer (data infrastructure, training).
fy_26_27: Data architecture design; satellite data pipeline scoping.
fy_27_28: Pilot integration in one model module; capacity building for research division.
fy_28_29: Full climate-augmented QPM with extended horizon operational.
rsf_fsap_link: Reinforces IMF RSF climate data infrastructure pillar.

title: Greening of monetary policy instruments — feasibility study
trigger: BNR conducts a feasibility assessment of climate-sensitive monetary policy tools (reserve requirements differentiation, collateral framework adjustments) in the context of the ongoing ECF-driven monetary instrument reform.
rationale: BNR managing live ECF reform (data-driven monetary policy framework, price-based auctions, exchange rate flexibility). NGFS adaptation co-chairmanship creates expectation of deliverables. 'Greening MP instruments' remains untouched but is the highest-profile axis internationally.

scalable_ambition.advanced: Adoption of one differentiated reserve requirement parameter or green collateral pilot.

ta: Long-term institutional — high political sensitivity, must be sequenced behind A1.1.
donor_complementarity: No active TA; positions AFD against NGFS / Banque de France-aligned expertise.
fy_27_28: Feasibility study completed; internal concept note approved.
rsf_fsap_link: Forward-looking — supports future RSF discussions on monetary policy greening.

title: Sovereign SLL issuance includes a climate-related KPI
trigger: Rwanda's next official creditor Sustainability-Linked Loan includes a formally agreed, independently verifiable climate-related Key Performance Indicator (e.g. forest cover, climate-resilient agriculture coverage) with defined Sustainability Performance Targets (SPTs) and an agreed verification methodology.
rationale: DG Debt confirmed active engagement on an existing SLF framework (WB-supported) with a narrow KPI set. Expanding to a climate KPI (forestry / NDC-aligned) would anchor the framework in Rwanda's highest-visibility sustainability commitment and set a regional precedent. AFD's Kenya SLF experience provides a direct peer reference. This DLI is a market-activation trigger: it requires a contracted financial arrangement, not just a policy document.

scalable_ambition.baseline: One climate KPI agreed and formally referenced in the next SLL term sheet.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Climate KPI package (2+ indicators) embedded in SLL + first independent verification completed.

ta: Short-term specialised (KPI calibration, SPT-setting methodology, AFD Kenya peer exchange) + medium-term verification support.
donor_complementarity: WB-RAMP supports reserves management; GIZ supports taxonomy. Neither covers the sovereign SLL instrument directly. AFD's Kenya SLF experience is a differentiating advantage.
fy_26_27: KPI methodology developed; SPT agreed with DG Debt; external verifier selected.
fy_27_28: Climate KPI formally referenced in official creditor SLL term sheet.
fy_28_29: First independent verification completed; SPT compliance assessed.
rsf_fsap_link: Supports IMF RSF sustainable debt management pillar; aligns with Article IV calls for climate KPI frameworks.
risks: Dependence on B1.2 data infrastructure for verification

title: National deforestation monitoring as climate finance data infrastructure
trigger: Rwanda operationalises a satellite-based national deforestation monitoring system producing annual district-level forest cover and restoration data, formally validated by NISR within the national environment statistics framework and suitable for use as a climate KPI baseline and independent verification methodology.
rationale: IMF Article IV 2025 flags climate data infrastructure as a binding cross-cutting constraint. No credible forestry KPI (B1.1) or forestry-anchored SLF framework (B1.3) is achievable without an independently verifiable baseline. NISR and REMA are willing counterparts. Satellite data capacity is nascent but exists (BNR data science team already uses satellite imagery for agricultural estimates). EU supports NISR environment data foundations — AFD builds on this with the finance-linked MRV dimension.

scalable_ambition.baseline: Satellite-based methodology validated; first national deforestation baseline produced.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Annual district-level monitoring operationalised; NISR publishes environment data report with forest cover time series.

ta: Short-term technical (satellite data pipeline design, remote sensing methodology) + long-term capacity building (NISR environment statistics team, REMA monitoring systems).
donor_complementarity: EU supports NISR environment data with REMA and Ministry of Environment — AFD adds the finance-linked MRV design dimension. Clear additionality. No overlap.
fy_26_27: Methodology designed; satellite data pipeline scoped; coordination with NISR / REMA / RFA formalised.
fy_27_28: First national deforestation baseline produced and validated; data sharing protocol with DG Debt agreed.
fy_28_29: Annual monitoring operational; first update published in NISR environment statistics report.
rsf_fsap_link: Directly addresses the IMF Article IV 2025 climate data infrastructure bottleneck; prerequisite for B1.1 SPT verification and B1.3 MRV.
risks: Coordination with EU-funded environment data work

title: Forestry-anchored SLF framework and first issuance
trigger: MINECOFIN formally expands the existing Sustainability-Linked Finance framework to include a forestry cover / restoration KPI (supported by B1.2 monitoring infrastructure), and Rwanda completes its first sovereign Sustainability-Linked Finance issuance under this expanded framework with independent third-party verification.
rationale: The existing SLF framework (WB-supported) provides the institutional architecture; B1.1 demonstrates the market activation logic; B1.2 delivers the MRV infrastructure. B1.3 is the integration layer — it turns policy and data into a contracted instrument. A forestry-anchored SLF issuance would directly mobilise climate finance against Rwanda's NDC 3.0 forest cover commitments and provide a landmark precedent in the EAC region.

scalable_ambition.baseline: SLF framework formally expanded with forestry KPI + first issuance under expanded framework.
scalable_ambition.advanced: Second issuance with updated forestry KPI and first verification cycle completed.

ta: Short-term (SLF framework legal expansion, issuance structuring, investor engagement) + long-term (framework maintenance, verification oversight).
donor_complementarity: Builds on WB SLF architecture and AFD Kenya SLF experience. LuxDev (RSE legal support) and GIZ (taxonomy) are complementary. Sequencing is explicit: B1.3 conditioned on B1.1 and B1.2.
fy_26_27: Legal analysis of SLF framework expansion; investor mapping; coordination with B1.1 and B1.2 teams.
fy_27_28: Expanded SLF framework legally formalised; first issuance structuring completed.
fy_28_29: First forestry-anchored SLF issuance completed; independent verification protocol activated.
rsf_fsap_link: Operationalises the IMF RSF sustainable debt management pillar; connects climate data (B1.2) to financial market outcomes.
risks: Sequencing dependency on B1.1 and B1.2

title: Regulatory framework for SACCO climate insurance distribution
trigger: BNR (as insurance regulator) issues a regulatory framework authorising and standardising the distribution of climate insurance products through the SACCO network, aligned with the National Insurance Strategy and the National DRF Strategy.
rationale: SACCOs are the natural last-mile channel for smallholder climate insurance; current regulatory architecture not yet adapted. Foundational to any product roll-out. Builds on WB-funded MSME Bridge Lending Window + macro parametric backstop (DRF Diagnostic / Strategy).

scalable_ambition.advanced: Framework + supervisory guidance + first SACCO licensed for distribution.

ta: Long-term institutional (MINECOFIN / BNR insurance supervision capacity + SACCO operational readiness).
fy_26_27: Regulatory framework drafted and circulated for consultation.
fy_28_29: First SACCO licensed for climate insurance distribution.
rsf_fsap_link: Supports IMF FSAP climate accountability dimension; complements WB DRF strategy.
risks: Supervisory capacity at BNR insurance directorate

rationale: Rwandan insurance market is small and individual underwriting capacity insufficient for systemic climate risk. Industry pool model could address this. Phase II adds market-structure dimension to the WB / GSFF financial mechanism.

scalable_ambition.advanced: Pool operational with capital + reinsurance arrangements.

donor_complementarity: No active donor on insurance pool architecture; complements WB / GSFF.
